summary:
# NOTES ON FIVE BOOKS (for later lookup)

## BOOK 1: A Little Irish Girl (J. M. Callwell)

**Cast:** Norah O'Brien (11, youngest, small, short black hair, blue "Irish" eyes, pretends Irish brogue, keeps "Irish" spelling of name with final h); Anstace O'Brien (elder sister, governess to Dr. Trafford's family; Mrs. Trafford); Roderick O'Brien (eldest, 21, Oxford-type honours, lawyer's clerk, cough, later writes for magazines, e.g. *Piccadilly*); Manus O'Brien (~12, school in Kent, Dr. Ford's school, later diphtheria); Piers O'Brien (father, journalist, died 6 months before book, illness after wet night); mother Marion Belthorpe (died at Norah's birth, per Anstace). Lily Allardyce (Norah's friend, pink, rich, Hampshire, Heron's Court; Paris trip). Treherne House school in north London: Miss Euphemia (junior teacher, pencil taps, high white cap), Miss Susan, eldest Miss Clarkson (severe, sanctum on landing), Fräulein Glock. Cousin Ansey (Anstace O'Brien, d. last week; fiancé Hugh Masters went to America, never returned; kept waiting; asylum in Dublin 12 years). Kilshane (small house on cliffs, 2 miles from Moyross, ~100 pounds/yr estate). Uncle Nicholas O'Brien (Moyross Abbey, copper mine, Drinane Head; feud; engaged to Marion Belthorpe; she eloped with Piers the day before wedding; father of Marion died of shock). Harry Wyndham (heir in Nicholas's view; Moyross; later Austria/Carpathians, army) and Ella Wyndham (his sister; pony Sheila; Miss Browne "Brownie" governess, from India, mother Mrs. Wyndham died of cholera). Biddy (cook; brother Tom Hogan, steward/gardener; 7 orphans incl. red-headed Lanty, Kat the baby, Bride the maid). Connor (car driver). Mr. & Mrs. Lynch (old rector, churchgoers; "boxed your father's ears"). Lady Louisa Butler (Dromore). Captain Lester, R.M. (magistrate). M'Bain (Scotch mine manager). Malachy Flanagan (red-bearded potheen maker, orator, Drinane Head). Cartwright (butler at Moyross); Mrs. Trafford.

**Events:**
- Ch1: Treherne House; geography lesson; Norah daydreams "Tuesday fortnight"; sent to bottom; Lily consoles. Norah's Irish pride. Piers's death; Lily goes to Paris, Norah stuck at school. Anstace visits.
- Ch2: Anstace announces inheritance of Kilshane. Uncle Nicholas feud explained. Roderick visited Moyross for funeral; Nicholas turned white, didn't speak. Dr. Trafford says Roderick's lungs delicate.
- Ch3: Norah, celebrating, tobogans down stairs on tea-tray with Lily; both fall; Norah bumps head. Miss Clarkson kisses Norah, lets her off ("little wild Irishwoman").
- Ch4: Sea-sickness voyage; Dublin; train to Ballyfin; outside car at night; roar of Atlantic; Tom Hogan carries Norah in; Biddy's welcome.
- Ch5: Kilshane explored; kitchen with hens and dog; Anstace's disgust; Biddy's stories of Miss Ansey; Lanty brings fish; Norah frees house from lumber.
- Ch6: Lynch & Lady Louisa; Manus's letter (diphtheria at school); Norah drives to meet Manus; Ella's pony Sheila bolts; Roderick catches her on bridge; Ella and Anstace friendship; Miss Browne's bonnet on backwards. Ella: "We are cousins."
- Ch7: Miss Browne's history; Harry's travels; Mr. O'Brien (Nicholas) asks Ella about O'Briens; portrait of Marion ("That is not the portrait of any O'Brien").
- Ch8: Lanty and Manus plan seal hunt in Ballintaggart Cave; Norah eavesdrops, follows; Manus kills seal with Roderick's gun; Lanty clubs it.
- Ch9: Return by Monk's Walk; Norah and Manus see white figure; Manus fires; it is a laundry table-cloth on tree; Miss Browne scolds maid. Manus and Norah keep secret.
- Ch10: Captain Lester (R.M.) to stay at Kilshane to raid Drinane Head still; Manus and Norah learn of still; Norah goes at dawn to warn Lanty.
- Ch11: Norah walks to Drinane Head alone; warns Lanty; Malachy hides her; "Stand her beside ye" under shawl.
- Ch12: Lester's raid fails; Roderick sees Norah; Malachy carries Norah home on his back.
- Ch13: Mr. Lester's dinner; Roderick & Anstace away at Dromore; Norah and Manus go to mine at dusk; Malachy harangues miners; they march on Moyross.
- Ch14: Harry returns to Moyross; Norah and Manus raise alarm; Norah makes ghost in abbey window with quilt, candle; mob flees. Mr. O'Brien (Nicholas) sees the figure, recalls Piers.
- Ch15: Norah falls from window, concussion; Ella nursing; Mr. O'Brien sends for doctor.
- Ch16: Recovery; Roderick and Ella engaged; Mr. O'Brien reconciles, will leave estate to Roderick as heir; Harry to army; Lanty promises to quit potheen, made under-keeper; Malachy's tears; Norah reveals table-cloth secret; Mr. O'Brien: "I wish your father Piers were here." Book ends a year after Piers's death.

## BOOK 2: The Boy Traders; or The Sportsman's Club Among the Boers (Harry Castlemon)

**Cast:** Frank Nelson (sailing master, young captain; Frank Nelson series); Uncle Dick (captain of the schooner *Stranger*, old sailor, meerschaum pipe, "Human natur'!" phrases); Walter Gaylord (paymaster, keeps key of strong box), Eugene Gaylord (brother, new Henry rifle, flute, impulsive), Archie Winters (cousin, joker, "I wasn't born"), Fred Craven, George Le Dell, Jasper Babcock, Phil Perkins, Chase, Wilson (Florida, absent), Dick Lewis (trapper, Indian yells, "Whoop!"), Bob Kelly (old trapper), Featherweight, Perk ("I'll tell you what's a fact"), Mr. Baldwin (first mate), Mr. Parker (second mate), Barton (coxswain/boatswain's mate), Lucas (old boatswain's mate), Rodgers, Tom Moone? (no—that's Book 4), Waters (convict giant; "Stand by me, mates!"), Brown (sailor), Stevens, Bob (ticket-of-leave convict), Fowler (consul's clerk, "Aw!"), Mack/McGregor (Scottish transport-rider, Natal guide, deserter), Mr. Wilbur (sheep-farmer, Tasmania), Mynheer Schrader (surly Boer, field cornet), Diego? (no), Mr. Jones (Frank's nickname for Griqua), Pedro? (no); Zulu chief; Griqua chief.

**Events:**
- Ch1: Sandwich Islands; Frank quizzed on cyclones by Uncle Dick; club recap (Walter captured by robbers; Archie rode wild horse; Frank's rise from forecastle); Hilo surf-board; Eugene dares Archie, both back off; Kilauea: trappers terrified; boys descend crater; trappers decide to follow Uncle Dick to Pacific islands and elephants.
- Ch2: Schooner shells Mangrove Island (Long Tom); gale; boys battened below; schooner dismasted; Frank saves crew; sailor swept.
- Ch3: Four weeks calm; cyclone approaches; Mr. Baldwin explains hurricanes; Uncle Dick turns away; storm; schooner dismantled; Long Tom (30-pounder) thrown overboard; reef passage; natives in canoes; 20-pounder shrapnel.
- Ch4: Sea Gull (English ship) wrecked; 11 men saved; four suspected convicts (Waters, others) from Van Diemen's Land; Frank fears giant Waters.
- Ch5: Waters insolent; Barton's warning about Waters asking about strong box; Waters strikes Lucas; Dick Lewis hurls him; Uncle Dick puts Waters in brig; 3 foremast hands pardoned.
- Ch6: Schooner reaches Hobart Town; Waters reveals destination; Fowler visits (consul's clerk); Dick and Bob confront; Mr. Wilbur.
- Ch7: Sheep station; Archie vs Dick race (Eugene's horse; Dick wins a race); Melbourne; horse stolen by bushrangers; return to Hobart; Fowler's questions about strong box.
- Ch8: Fowler and Bob seize schooner at night; Frank locked in cabin; Waters, Fowler, Bob; Frank's plan; revealed motive: Walter's key and money.
- Ch9: Fowler tries to lure Walter; Archie seized by Bob by mistake; Waters interrogates Frank; schooner escapes steamer by night trick.
- Ch10: Archie irons Waters while sleeping; recaptures ship; Frank orders Yankee tricks; war steamer; English lieutenant; Frank refuses to haul flag.
- Ch11: Midshipman Kendall; flag incident; convicts taken; Uncle Dick and Wilbur recover ship via tug; Frank's stubbornness praised; three sailors discharged; new men shipped; voyage to Natal.
- Ch12: Natal (Port Natal/Grahamstown); English colonel's outfit (oxen, wagon, horses, elephant guns); Mack hired; lots for horses/guns (Frank draws "crowbait" and heavy #3 rifle; Archie gets thoroughbred and silver-mounted rifle); Kaffir servants.
- Ch13: Boer farmer Schrader refuses trade; Griqua gun repair; Mack's warnings; lion veldt; Eugene's challenge to shooting-hole.
- Ch14: Night in shooting-pit at spring; jackal; lions (troop); firing; Uncle Dick arrives.
- Ch15: Dead wild dog, not lion; Kaffirs plan desertion; Archie's horse found; Mack stealing gun at night.
- Ch16: Mack deserts with Walter's horse and Uncle Dick's double-barrel; "We're deserted"; trek; Griqua village; Zulu embassy demands rifle; Dick's war dance and yells scares Zulu chief away.
- Ch17: Griqua "medicine-man" Dick; Zulu attack in ravine; Archie's horse killed; Frank saves Archie's cousin; Boers resume trade; Mack sold horse/gun in Grahamstown; home to Bellville; epilogue on each member's later life (Frank a lawyer, Archie civil engineer married, Fred revenue lieutenant, Walter and Eugene plantation).

## BOOK 3: "In Sargasso" Missing (Julius Chambers)

**Cast:** Capt. Austin Clark (narrator; American, Brooklyn; Black Ball line, Cameron & Co.; captain of Caribas); Caribas (tramp steamer, owned by Triplett & Jones, Plymouth); Arthur Gray (pretended artist, Secor launch, Sargasson agent, born in US, formerly Englishman abandoned by his crew); the Kantoon (commander of Happy Shark, ~60, grizzly beard, stands in barrel of water, polyglot speech); Fidette (his daughter; hazel-brown eyes, auburn hair, sea-grass dress; mother a New Orleans Creole, from ship George Cornwall, Capt. Timothy Rogers); Fernandez Otranto (Portuguese, trombone, from Royal George/Green Octopod ex-Franklin ship); Hansko Yap (young rebel, spar battering ram); Chin-Goone (1816 rebel); Donna Elenora (Kantoon of Cormorant's wife); the Chief Kantoon; High Priest of Sacred Fire; Priest; Deputy Chief Kantoon; Unk-ta-hee (barge); cabin boy (killed); boatswain (killed by drowning in water-butt); Brown (sailor); Stevens; the Doctor (negro cook); Lascar; Jem? no.

**Events:**
- Ch1-2: Preface (Sargasso Sea, 22°-28°N, 25°-60°W); Caribas sailed from New York in June for Azores; Clark accepts passenger Gray; diverts to Sargasso; mirage of ships; Clark goes in launch with Gray; oars dropped; Gray steals rifle; launch engine fails.
- Ch3: Gray betrays Clark; Clark's cartridge belt dropped; taken aboard Happy Shark; Kantoon; cell with carvings.
- Ch4: Gray explains Sargasson loyalty; Clark's rage; sleepless night.
- Ch5: Sargasson customs; polyglot Kantoon; history of Sargassons (Armada origin, slave ship, intermarriage); death-chant and extinction rules.
- Ch6: Red "Sacred Fire" light; attack on Caribas planned; Sargasson Tabasco-type powder; boatswain's warning; attack and seizure of Caribas; crew killed; boat-boys.
- Ch7: Boatswain's last stand; drowned in water-butt; cabin boy thrown overboard; Clark despair.
- Ch8: Fidette brings food, sprig of bay; her mother's story; Clark kisses her.
- Ch9: Kantoon angry; Fidette's history; Kantoon's wife, the Creole; Fidette's education; Sargasson law (death for extinction, marriage custom).
- Ch10: Kitchen-ship cooking; barnacle soup; Caribas moored nearby.
- Ch11: Fidette and Clark on bowsprit; Fidette's lost love Fernandez.
- Ch12: Clark jealous; Fidette rejects him; Fernandez's trombone heard.
- Ch13: "Week of Silence" festival; Dance of the Derelicts.
- Ch14: Fernandez visits; no bluefish scale; Fidette douses him with water; Fernandez drowned in sack by order of Kantoon.
- Ch15: Visiting women; Chin-Goone rebellion history; Hansko Yap threat.
- Ch16: Papier-mâché orange bombs (Wilmington, Del. fireworks) in Kantoon's cabin; Hansko Yap's rebel crew; spar of Happy Shark.
- Ch17-18: Spar fight; Kantoon killed (hamstrung by Lascar); Fidette climbs masthead, drops bombs; attackers destroyed; Fidette recaptured ship.
- Ch19: Survivors hide under spar; Clark buries Kantoon; Clark claims kantoonship; civil marriage at mainmast; Kantoon's funeral.
- Ch20: Making new boats from root cables; sea-root telegraph; Clark's pilfering the Ceylon idea; fire on ship.
- Ch21-22: Summoned by High Priest (Unk-ta-hee); "Chief Kantoon's" tea of gold; ceremony with hot marlinspike; Clark named Kantoon of Caribas.
- Ch23: Return to Caribas; Gray seized.
- Ch24: Gray killed in drowning chair; "Let him walk with God."
- Ch25-26: Fidette and Donna Elenora "woman question" reform; gig; Donna Elenora steals flint from priest; Sacred Light alarm.
- Ch27: Priest's Sacred Flint stolen; Clark gives flints (heavy rocks with "fire" sparks).
- Ch28-29: Escape plan; engine repaired; knife-grinder song; prisoners locked; steam raised; Caribas escapes.
- Ch30: Steaming north; fuel out; picked up by German steamer Nordland; arrives New York (Horseshoe); telegram: "Proceed Santos, then Buenos Ayres for orders." Tripplett & Jones.

## BOOK 4: For God and Gold (Julian Corbett)

**Narrator:** Jasper Festing (Longdene, Kent; Trinity College, Cambridge; later Drake's merchant/gentleman adventurer; "Mr. Festing"). Preface by editor.

**Cast:** Nicholas Festing (father, Puritan wool-merchant, d. January, Elizabeth's first year); Cicely (nurse) & Miles (steward, Lashmer's father); Lashmer (servant, Miles's son); Sir Fulke Waldyve (old knight, Ashtead; guardian; d. 1566-ish); Harry Waldyve (friend/brother, later married to Nan St. John; Italianate, went to Italy, Berwick, Lord Russell's household); Mr. Drake (Thomas/Ned, Puritan preacher, Chatham; hulk on the Medway); Mrs. Drake (wife); sons John (Jack), Joseph (Joe), Frank (Francis), James, Willie (youngest); Mr. Death (sour preacher); Mr. Follet (scholarly tutor, "Apology"); Mr. Cartwright (Thomas, Puritan fellow of Trinity); Dr. Beaumont (Master of Trinity; brother John Beaumont Vice-Master); Saunderson (Fasting Johnnie); Dr. Baker (King's Provost); Dr. Whitgift (later Master); Dr. Medcalfe; Culverin (Sergeant Alexander Culverin, "schiavona," moustache, Signor John Peter Pugliano); Nan St. John (Mrs. Waldyve, ruddy hair, brown eyes, Lord Bedford's niece); Fulke Waldyve (infant son); Mr. Oxenham (John, fellow adventurer, hanged later in Lima); Captain Ranse (Lion); John Overy (master of Lion); Captain Tetú (French); Tom Moone (carpenter of Swan); Allen (quartermaster); Robert; Diego (Cimaroon); Pedro (Cimaroon chief); Strammers? no. Calmenaras, Nicuese (historical); Señorita (Spanish girl, Gasparo, "Dragon Francisco"); Ellis Hixom (master); Sir Edward Horsey; Captain David Carlet; Jack Garrett; Mr. John Hawkins; Captain Lovell; Gov. Don Martin Henriquez.

**Events in order:**
- Preface/prologue. Ch1: Jasper's youth at Longdene; father's death; Cicely's report; Miles's deference. Harry's childhood; Sir Fulke's friendship with Nicholas.
- Ch2: Harry gives gilded hawk-bells; Sir Fulke's rage at Cicely; Drake and Death arrive with father's will; Drake insists on Reformation funeral; Sir Fulke allows; funeral at moss-grown Longdene church; Paternoster sung; Drake's oration.
- Ch3: Rochester; Drake's capstan sermon; Drake's house on hulk (Medway); Drake's boys fight; Frank name-dropped; Mr. Follet's tutoring; Follet's Apology; boys' wonder at West Indies.
- Ch4: Sir Fulke's courtly training; Jasper and Harry depart for Cambridge; Gravesend farewell; Trinity; Follet's lament; Jasper's fight with Oxenham-type brawl (effigy); Mr. Cartwright's conversion; Follet leaves.
- Ch5: Queen Elizabeth's visit to Cambridge (August 1564); Cartwright's oration; Lord Robert Dudley's visit; Jasper's ague; leaves Cambridge.
- Ch6: Harry (Ashtead); Frank Drake's boat *Gazehound*; Spanish-caravel piracy; Jasper's conscience; Frank's crew; Harry's Italian talk.
- Ch7: Caravel seized (Netherlanders, Spanish silks), Spanish gentleman killed by Jasper's rapier; Frank's meeting with *Minion* (Captain David Carlet); Mrs. Drake's lament; Jasper resolves to report Frank.
- Ch8: Frank's piracy defended; Jasper and Frank discuss licence; Jasper studies with Frank at Longdene; Harry leaves for Italy; Cambridge; Sir Fulke's death (Catholic priest).
- Ch9: Drake preacher Upnor; Hawkins voyage; Culverin's arrival; Frank's account of San Juan de Ulloa (Hawkins's betrayal, Frank abandons Jesus); Frank's grand plan for Nombre de Dios.
- Ch10: Harry marries Nan St. John; Jasper's jealousy; Puritan wars; Harry's Italian philosophy; Nan and Jasper talk; Culverin's comedy.
- Ch11: Jasper and Nan at Upchurch; Mr. Death in pulpit; Drake's sermon; communion; Jasper seduces Nan's faith.
- Ch12: Frank's new voyage; Harry declines; Nan's despair; Jasper kisses her; "lust of the spirit."
- Ch13: Inn at Rochester; Harry discovers them; Harry flings rapier through window; Jasper snaps own blade, kisses Harry's rapier; oath.
- Ch14: Nan's song; letter to Nan from Harry (30 April 1572); Jasper seeks Follet; London.
- Ch15: St Paul's brawl; Frank and Oxenham rescue Jasper; Frank's plan.
- Ch16: Frank's voyage fitting out; Harry and Jasper reconcile at Plymouth; Frank's sermon.
- Ch17: Atlantic crossing; Canaries; Guadeloupe; Port Pheasant; Garrett's warning plate; Anchor fort; Captain Ranse consort ("Consortship" articles, 13 July 1572).
- Ch18: Night attack on Nombre de Dios (Cimaroon Pedro ally; Frank's "great captain" speech); Frank wounded; town taken; "Treasure-House"; silver bars; bell; storm; Frank wounded in boot.
- Ch19: Sergeant Culverin looting; Frank's Spanish envoy; Frank scuttles Swan (Tom Moone's gimlet); Frank's policy.
- Ch20: Port Plenty; Cimaroon village; Diego; Frank's "Diego" plan; Harry's fort; Culverin supervising; Allen's mutiny, John Drake dies.
- Ch21: Mosquitoes; sickness; Joseph dies; Frank's dissection of Joe with Vicary's *Anglishman's Treasure*; Spanish girl (Señorita) captured; Jasper guards her.
- Ch22: South Sea sighted; march over isthmus; Cimaroon guidance; Harry & Jasper talk; Panama reconnoitred; Sergeant's aqua vitae.
- Ch23: Mule train ambush fails (Culverin drunk, horse neighs, spoils); Treasurer of Lima's train turned back; mule trains taken on road; Venta Cruz; Panama fight with monks; Pedro cuts horse soldiers.
- Ch24: Retreat; Sergeant punished on hobby-horse; Veragua plans; Jasper's romance with Señorita (kisses); Frank's news of Massacre of Paris (St Bartholomew); Frenchman Tetú.
- Ch25: Jasper parts with Señorita; Cimaroon attack; Carthagena ambush; Sergeant leads cavalry rush; huge silver recua taken; buried silver; Tetú left behind.
- Ch26: Pinnaces captured; Jasper and Harry; Harry gives up honour; Jasper's Señorita; Frank's raft; storm; pinnaces found at Cabeças.
- Ch27: Señorita's hammock; Oxenham's rivalry; Señorita's confession (married old man); Jasper refuses; she departs in boat; Oxenham sails *Pasha* away.
- Ch28: Oxenham's end (hanged at Lima); Frank's return to Plymouth (9 August 1573); Frank's sermon; Harry and Jasper ride to Ashtead; Nan's welcome; Culverin dies later; Jasper's life after.

## BOOK 5: The O'Ruddy: A Romance (Stephen Crane & Robert Barr)

**Narrator:** Tom O'Ruddy (of Glandore, Co. Cork; head of ancient branch; "The O'Ruddy"; pride, duel-prone).

**Cast:** Father (The O'Ruddy elder, d. 3 weeks earlier; gave Tom two swords (King Louis's grand sword), papers for Lord Strepp, breeches loan in France); Earl of Westport (old; was Lord Strepp in France; bright shrewd eyes; cackling; "Straw!"); Countess (ogress, carries ebony stick, "Hoity-Toity"); Lady Mary Strepp (daughter; beautiful; later Tom's wife); Arthur, Lord Strepp (son, ~20, fair hair, honorable); Colonel Clarence Royale (old, gout, Ponsonby? swordsman, friend of Lord Strepp); Reginald Forister (black-skinned, shipping partner of Earl, duellist; "Nell"; child); Paddy (red-headed Irish servant, flame-hair, stolen papers, duel helper, "Mickey"); Jem Bottles (highwayman, seven ballads in Bristol, three in Bath, mother who scolds; "stand and deliver"); Doctor Chord (little scientist, scandal-monger, blunderbuss-fearing, gossip); Father Donovan (Tom's priest, Glandore, going to Rome); Mickey Clancy (steward at Glandore); Josiah Brooks (lawyer, Temple); Strammers (gardener with blunderbuss, "French pears"); Fullbil, Bobbs, Fancher (London wits at "Pig and Turnip"); Sir Edmund Flixton; Tom Peel (Rye giant smuggler, captain of 9 men); Father Kilnane; Patsy O'Gorman (dead miser); Sir Goddard Oxenbridge (ghost at Brede); Hoity-Toity.

**Events:**
- Ch1: Glandore history; father's death; Tom sails to Bristol; "Papers" for Earl; Bristol inn; Lord Strepp & Col. Royale mock father's stolen breeches story; Tom's challenge; kicks Forister down the inn steps; Earl bumps; Tom says "The O'Ruddy."
- Ch2: Keening Irishman (Paddy) found; duel at dawn; Paddy dressed as Tom's second in flowery waistcoat and lashings-talk; Tom stops after Royale wounded; duel spared, Royale in four places.
- Ch3: Papers missing; Forister suspected; Paddy stole them (for Mary? no—"Boots"); chase; Jem Bottles robs Tom on road; Paddy's Bath escapade; papers found on Paddy? Jem Bottles & Paddy; "Mrs. Bottles."
- Ch4: Tom's infatuation with Lady Mary; Forister in Bath; Paddy catches "little black man" in Bath inn; Tom meets Earl's valet.
- Ch5: Forister at Bristol; Lord Strepp's partner; Tom meets Lord Strepp & Col. Royale reconciled; Earl in bed: "Straw!"; Lady Mary enters; Earl accuses Tom of ruining him.
- Ch6: Tom returns papers, Earl's fit; Strepp: "Forister is my father's partner"; Forister's duel threat; Royale's bet.
- Ch7: Forister visits Tom; "Nell" blackmail; Tom's mock ruse; Lord Strepp & Royale part.
- Ch8: Countess and Lady Mary in garden; parrot; Countess attacks Tom with chairs; Lady Mary's tearful "don't fight Forister."
- Ch9: Duel at dawn; Tom wins by pricking Forister's shoulder; Forister carried off; Royale's "Mary's bath"; "God spare you" notes.
- Ch10: Tom's fame; Countess chases Tom around table; Tom escapes.
- Ch11: Forister's pallor; Tom's inn; Paddy & Jem with papers (stolen from carriage; "Dear Sister Mary" letter); Tom returns Paddy and Jem's money; Tom pledges to return papers.
- Ch12: Bath; Earl's wounded pride; Tom threatens with papers; Earl's "I'll have you gaoled"; Tom in London.
- Ch13: Earl's chamber; "Why not read the papers?" Tom: "I thought a tutor"; Lady Mary's "Father Donovan"? ; Tom's exit.
- Ch14: Countess locked in room by Paddy with chair; Paddy and Tom flee; Paddy's Bantry lore.
- Ch15: Ride to London; Tom and Paddy's dialogue about England; Paddy's duty of mimicry; Bottles's lore.
- Ch16: Inn at Chichester? ; Jem and Paddy taught to be servants; "sticadoro" fencing questions.
- Ch17: London arrival; "Pig and Turnip" inn; Paddy's hair cut; Jem and Paddy under watch.
- Ch18: Fullbil's coffeehouse (Bobbs, Fancher, Chord); Tom insulted; "Ireland not in Italy"; Flixton; Tom tells story of "King of Galway."
- Ch19: Paddy & Jem at Red Slipper mug-house; Paddy dresses as gentleman; the "loriot" bird talk.
- Ch20: Kensington Gardens; Chord's gossip; Lady Mary sighted; eye-contact; Tom follows.
- Ch21: Chord's gossip; Earl's house plans; Tom wants to climb tree; Doctor Chord's "gill of port" speech.
- Ch22: Tom attempts speech with Lady Mary; locked; Earl's gardener; Lady Mary's "father's papers" — Tom and Chord plan climbing tree to Earl's garden at 10 a.m. Chord bolts; Strammers catches Tom with blunderbuss; Lady Mary intercedes; Tom declares love.
- Ch23: Strammers unbribed; Paddy & Jem bribe Strammers; Tom & Chord; plan for garden entry.
- Ch24: Strammers's invite; Tom's entry: Paddy and Jem beaten by household; Tom enters house; Lady Mary in boudoir; papers "kicked" to floor; Lady Mary consents to marry.
- Ch25: Lady Mary's letter to Mr. Josiah Brooks; papers left with Brooks; Brooks gives 500 guineas in gold; Tom returns to Father Donovan; Doctor Chord's betrayal; the bogus papers; nine swordsmen ambush and yield swords.
- Ch26: Brooks's office; "five hundred golden guineas"; Tom hires Paddy & Jem; Rye; Father Donovan.
- Ch27: Road to Rye; Jem robs nine highwaymen (saddles pile); Paddy beaten again; Maidstone; Rye.
- Ch28: Tom hires Tom Peel and eight smugglers; Brede House (Earl's estate in Sussex); Oxenbridge tunnel; Lord Strepp's attack; Brede defended with blunderbusses.
- Ch29: Lord Strepp captured in tunnel; Tom and Strepp talk; Strepp's sister; Paddy falls through trapdoor; Earl arrives; Countess; Lady Mary consents; Tom marries Lady Mary by Father Donovan; children Patrick, Mary, Terence, Kathleen, Michael, Bridget, Donovan. Narration ends.

Note: Ch numbering is editorial; Book 5 uses chapter headings I–XXXIII.
